context_purpose: A women-only bath area needs to keep out people who are not eligible and staff want some safety record.

norm_violation_today.reason: Recording ID numbers and face-and-ID photos in a logbook goes beyond a one-bit eligibility check and links named people to a bath visit.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: A named record for investigating an incident in the changing room, and any check that the holder is the person at the door (the proof is not bound to a face).

transmission_check.reason: The logbook is a staff habit for safety, not something I know any rule requiring, so a count-only gate looks lawful, though I am not certain of local bath regulations.

context_purpose: A promoter wants each ticket used by a real single buyer to stop bulk scalping with stolen identities.

norm_violation_today.reason: Keeping ID number, face template, device identifiers and reusing them for marketing goes beyond the anti-fraud purpose of gate matching.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Dispute handling, refunds, ticket transfer and a way to pursue a scalper after the fact; uniqueness alone does not cap per-person quantity unless the nullifier is per event.

transmission_check.reason: Real-name ticketing may be a regulator or venue requirement for some events, and I cannot say whether it requires retaining the ID itself.

context_purpose: An urban renewal organiser must confirm that each voter owns land in the renewal zone.

norm_violation_today.reason: A shared sheet of owners' names, IDs and home addresses circulated among volunteers goes well beyond the eligibility purpose.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Share ratios and lot identity, which ownership-weighted consent counts and later disputes probably need.

transmission_check.reason: Consent thresholds for renewal are set by law by ownership share and the formal process probably needs auditable owner records, which I cannot confirm.

context_purpose: A licence holder must show that every alcohol sale from the machine was age-checked.

norm_violation_today.reason: Storing passport or ID numbers, birth date and nationality in a notebook goes beyond an age check that needs no copy.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Little; the log line proves a check was accepted but the inspector cannot independently re-identify the buyer in a dispute.

transmission_check.reason: An age check is plainly required but I do not know whether the inspector expects stored identity data.

context_purpose: A disaster shelter needs quickly to know that a volunteer nurse is currently licensed before giving her a clinical role.

norm_violation_today.reason: Posting licence and ID photos to a LINE group and keeping them on a personal phone exposes ID number, address and birth date to many people.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Identification for the shelter head-count and for accountability if care goes wrong; the proof covers only the role decision.

transmission_check.reason: This is an informal ad hoc practice, not a known legal duty, so a freshness proof is allowed if the infrastructure works.

context_purpose: A library runs a children's reading program and wants eligibility, attendance statistics and one prize per child.

norm_violation_today.reason: A visit log tying guardian ID number and child details across weeks is more than eligibility and prize caps require.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Contact for prize pickup or safety follow-up, and the per-child nullifier is hard to design without any stable identifier.

transmission_check.reason: Families hand details over voluntarily for a free program and no duty to keep them is evident.

context_purpose: Existing tenants want some assurance that a prospective flatmate is not dangerous.

norm_violation_today.reason: Strangers keep an ID photo and full criminal record certificate indefinitely in a group chat, which exceeds the one-bit need.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: The detail of an offence (type, date) that tenants might weigh, and the register named may not exist as a citizen-checkable list.

transmission_check.reason: No law obliges private tenants to collect the record, so a narrower proof is allowed if an issuer offers it.

context_purpose: A public library must confirm that an adult is a guardian of a child under the card's age limit.

norm_violation_today.reason: Copying a household transcript exposes parents, spouses, siblings and address when only a guardian-of-child fact is needed.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Informal custody cases such as grandparents not registered as guardians, plus a stable card number that is anyway issued by the library.

transmission_check.reason: The transcript requirement looks like desk practice rather than a known statutory duty, so I expect a narrower proof to be accepted.
